source.title: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection

verified_claims.claim: ALFWorld single-pass RSEA 69.3% vs ReAct 64.6%, McNemar p=0.015; retry RSEA 79.4%.
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. Scope: ALFWorld, 134 tasks × 5 seeds, Qwen2.5-7B as reported.

verified_claims.claim: Dynamic Cheatsheet is near-best on ALFWorld at 70.7% but collapses on WebShop to 0.136 vs ReAct 0.429; it is also worst among listed methods on tau-bench at 36.7% vs ReAct 41.7%.
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. This is direct benchmark-scoped evidence of negative transfer/context distraction for this unguarded method; it is not evidence that all unguarded context evolution necessarily fails.

verified_claims.claim: On WebShop every evolved RSEA candidate hurt held-out validation, so the frozen state is empty; RSEA 0.437 vs ReAct 0.429.
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. Supports the fallback behavior in this benchmark/configuration.

verified_claims.claim: Selection ablation: no held-out gate gives 100.0% in-sample and 66.7% test; strict-gate RSEA gives 67.3% test; ReAct empty-state control 63.6%.
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. The paper describes this as a 33-point train–test gap for the no-gate state.

verified_claims.claim: Layer ablation: ReAct 64.2; strategy 67.3; skills 69.8; playbook 69.8; strategy+skills 67.9; full RSEA 68.5.
verified_claims.assessment: Verified. The paper explicitly says the layers overlap and should not be read as three orthogonal/individually necessary signals.

corrections_or_clarifications.verified_scope: The paper's 'monotone-safe' claim is tied to the strict held-out selection procedure and the sampled held-out validation distribution. The authors explicitly note that small/unrepresentative validation draws can still allow harmful ties under non-strict selection and that transfer benchmarks use modest evaluation sizes/single shuffled split in some cases. Do not reinterpret this as a universal guarantee over unseen distributions.

Evidence does not support a claim that strategy, skills, and playbook are all necessary or complementary. Individual concrete layers carry most of the benefit and the full combination is not best in the reported layer ablation.

The held-out-vs-no-gate ablation on ALFWorld directly supports reduced overfitting under that setup. The severe WebShop Dynamic-Cheatsheet failure is a separate cross-method negative-transfer comparison, not a matched RSEA gate-removal experiment on WebShop. Keep these evidence types distinct.

unresolved_gaps: No independent replication was verified in this run.

The paper's strongest safety language should remain bounded to its validation/test setup; repeated adaptive reuse of the same validation split and nonstationary deployment are not established by these results.

downstream_action.integrator: May treat the strict held-out selection ablation, WebShop negative-transfer example, fallback behavior, and overlapping-layer result as primary-verified only within the benchmark/configuration scopes above.
downstream_action.evidence_comparator: Keep direct gate ablation evidence separate from cross-method Dynamic-Cheatsheet failure evidence; independent replication remains absent.

next_verification: self_improvement/C4 KSI exact quantitative tables and component isolation, then MetaSkill-Evolve primary ablations.
